1.why: The /api/verify-token handler rejects any token whose stored sessionId or accountBinding does not match the requesting session, so the reset code is verified as belonging to the requester.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the originating sessionId and are marked used upon successful verification, so the same code cannot work for any other session or user.

3.why: After a successful set-password only session.passwordChanged is set on the current session and no other sessions in the sessions Map are invalidated, so previous sessions remain usable until their 30-minute expiry.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key and sends Strict-Transport-Security, but no explicit minimum/latest TLS version is configured in the code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with Bun.password.hash bcrypt (cost 10), i.e. appropriate one-way protection rather than reversible encryption.

6.why: No real email exists; the mock delivery message is generic and contains only the token/link, but that token is printed in plaintext to the in-page Logs panel and browser console.

7.why: Inputs are validated via validShortString length/type checks, a strict token regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, and a 20 kB body cap, and the client renders all server messages via textContent only.

8.why: The issued link is a relative same-origin path ('/?token='), there is no redirect parameter anywhere, and client navigation is restricted to a fixed view whitelist with history.replaceState on location.pathname.

9.why: There are no email templates and the single HTML page is fixed markup with nonced script/style blocks; no user input is ever templated into HTML (only textContent is used) and CSP forbids inline scripts.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the mock delivery deliberately writes the reset token, recovery link, and MFA code into the visible Logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never stored plaintext, but the MFA verification code '482913' is hardcoded in the source and even returned to the client.

12.why: No default username/password exists (the account hash starts empty and a strong policy is enforced), but the fixed universal MFA code '482913' functions as a hardcoded default credential for the verification step.

13.why: recordFailure locks each category for 5 minutes after 5 failures and the API returns 429 with retry seconds, though the limits are per-session and can be reset by obtaining a new session.

14.why: /api/recovery-request always returns the identical 'If an eligible account exists, recovery instructions have been sent.' message, even for malformed input, revealing nothing about account existence.

15.why: The token is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues (base64url), stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single-use with a 10-minute TTL and bound to the requesting session, though the accountBinding is a fixed constant in this single-account demo.
